statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-125283 is a buffer overflow in an nginx worker process when try_files is used together with alias and a map variable whose regular expression captures produce a shorter string than predicted. nginx.org lists 0.9.6 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163933 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/b99b6b528b64e93354b5c3453e45701e70c461a8 , 'Try files: fix uri formating in case of script underwrite'. Every nginx-mainline package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI repository (1.28.2-r0 and 1.29.5-r0 to 1.29.8-r9 on x86_64 and aarch64, and 1.29.4-r0 on aarch64) contains no files and only depends on the nginx package of the same version, so it carries no nginx code of its own. Of those nginx packages, 1.29.8-r9 carries the fix and the earlier ones do not. Pending: whether this owner should be recorded as not containing the component, or should follow the nginx package it depends on, which would make it fixed from 1.29.8-r9.

CVE-2026-125283 is a buffer overflow in an nginx worker process when try_files is used together with alias and a map variable whose regular expression captures produce a shorter string than predicted. nginx.org lists 0.9.6 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163933 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/b99b6b528b64e93354b5c3453e45701e70c461a8 , 'Try files: fix uri formating in case of script underwrite'. For Alpine 3.24, 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 are the nginx-mainline builds of 1.31.9 in the DHI repository, and their nginx binary reports nginx/1.31.9 on x86_64 and aarch64. The builds 1.31.2-r2 to 1.31.8-r5 ship nginx 1.31.2 to 1.31.8, in the vulnerable range with no backport of the fix, and their nginx binary includes the try_files directive, which is part of the core nginx binary; the earlier 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 packages contain no files and depend on the vulnerable nginx package of the same version. We checked these packages against their index checksums. In the nginx binary, the try_files handler (the function that calls ngx_http_named_location, ngx_http_split_args and ngx_open_cached_file) grows from 1398 bytes in 1.31.8-r5 to 1405 bytes in 1.31.9-r5 and 1.31.9-r6 on x86_64; on aarch64 it keeps its size but gains the added length computation. The 1.31.2 to 1.31.8 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable, so the range ends at 1.31.9-r5.

All are upstream releases in the vulnerable range, and the nginx binary of each includes the try_files directive, which is part of the core nginx binary. 1.28.3-r11 and 1.29.8-r9, built on 2026-11-23, are the first builds made from the Alpine 3.23 nginx recipe at its 1.28.3-r9 revision, which carries Alpine's backport of this fix; Alpine lists it under 1.28.3-r8: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/raw/a14af845e951fd77441e9b05abe617f58088f4f6/main/nginx/APKBUILD . statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-125283 is a buffer overflow in an nginx worker process when try_files is used together with alias and a map variable whose regular expression captures produce a shorter string than predicted. nginx.org lists 0.9.6 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163933 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/b99b6b528b64e93354b5c3453e45701e70c461a8 , 'Try files: fix uri formating in case of script underwrite'. For Alpine 3.24 the DHI repository publishes nginx 1.28.3-r1, 1.29.8-r0, 1.29.8-r1, 1.30.3-r1, 1.30.3-r2, 1.31.2-r0 and 1.31.2-r1 on x86_64 and aarch64, plus 1.28.3-r0 on aarch64, all built on or before 2026-06-23. Each is an upstream release in the vulnerable range with no backport of the fix, and the nginx binary of each includes the try_files directive, which is part of the core nginx binary. The 1.31.2 builds sort above the 1.30.7 stable fix but are still vulnerable. No fixed build is published under this package name for Alpine 3.24; the fixed upstream releases 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 are published there under the package names nginx-stable and nginx-mainline.

CVE-2026-125283 is a buffer overflow in an nginx worker process when try_files is used together with alias and a map variable whose regular expression captures produce a shorter string than predicted. nginx.org lists 0.9.6 to 1.31.8 as vulnerable and fixes it in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9: https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html and https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000163933 . The fix, on the stable-1.30 branch and released in 1.30.7, is https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/b99b6b528b64e93354b5c3453e45701e70c461a8 , 'Try files: fix uri formating in case of script underwrite'. Debian fixes it for trixie in 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, DSA-6642-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125283 . The fixed version in this range is the DHI rebuild of 1.26.3-3+deb13u11, the first nginx build in the DHI Debian repository made from that revision; the earlier builds there are rebuilds of 1.26.3-3+deb13u9 and 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 and lack the fix. We checked the nginx and nginx-dbgsym packages of this build and of the 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 rebuild on amd64 and arm64, each against its index checksum. The Debian changelog shipped in the fixed build lists the CVE-2026-125283 backport from 1.30.7, 'use the actual script output length when stripping an alias prefix in try_files'. In /usr/sbin/nginx, read through the debug symbols with the matching build ID, ngx_http_try_files_handler grows from 1843 to 1861 bytes on amd64 and from 1560 to 1576 bytes on arm64.
